**Style Notes:** Inside-out offense with talented bigs and versatile guards around them; traditional play style and drive and kick flow to create spontaneous advantages.

::::

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card title="Overview/Identity" fill="false"}

Old Dominion plays through an inside-out identity built around Riley Stack’s high-post presence, downhill creation from Dalanna Carter and Trinity Vance, and consistent movement around their bigs. They use 4-out 1-in spacing, high-post fills, weakside exchanges, empty-corner ball screens, and early transition attacks to create paint touches before flowing into secondary action. Their guards can create off the bounce, while Stack and Brackens provide screening, sealing, rim-running, and face-up options that keep the offense connected. Defensively, Old Dominion leans heavily on Stack as a rim protector in deep drop, mixes in 1-2-1-1 pressure back to 2-3, and plays with strong perimeter denial while collapsing aggressively from the weakside on paint touches. Their identity is built around size at the rim, pressure around the perimeter, and forcing opponents to make quick decisions against changing coverages.

::::

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .three-keys title="Three Keys" fill="false"}

<div class="keys-grid">

<div class="key-item"><span class="key-number">1</span><strong>Stop early paint touches from Carter and Vance and keep Stack from establishing easy high-post catches.</strong></div>

<div class="key-item"><span class="key-number">2</span><strong>Attack Stack in ball screens, use the space in deep drop, and force her to defend away from the rim.</strong></div>

<div class="key-item"><span class="key-number">3</span><strong>Stay patient against pressure and weakside collapse, maintain spacing, and keep the ball moving to force rotations.</strong></div>

</div>

# Personnel

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .player-card title="Shadasia Brackens" fill="false"}

::: {.player-meta}

**Role:** Stretch big

**Identity:** Power forward who can score at all three levels and run the floor in transition.

:::

#### Tendencies

- Loves to attack right from the perimeter
- Used out of pop + attack in BLOB
- Will look to spin out of her drives to get to jumper

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Guard Her

- Force drives to the left off high post catch or perimeter pop
- Maintain ball pressure to get ball on the floor and stunt attacks from high post

:::

#### Numbers

- Only 3 spot-up 3s taken this season
- 12 drives right vs. 1 drive left (0.833 PPP on right drives)
- 42% on dribble jumpers (43% TS%)

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .player-card title="Riley Stack" fill="false"}

::: {.player-meta}

**Role:** Primary post 5 who can stretch the floor

**Identity:** Versatile big who is physical in low post and works well around her guards from high post

:::

#### Tendencies

- Catches in high post or low block similar to Brackens
- Favors left side off attacks from FT line
- Screen + seals off-ball especially in middle of the floor and patient in her keeps
- Hard rolls off empty-corner ball screen but patient depending on coverage

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Guard Her

- Be physical and front when positioned under the basket
- Force right off high post catch and maintain high hands

:::

#### Numbers

- 13 post-ups with 0.923 PPP
- 7/9 drives to her left with 1.714 PPP
- 36/44 FGA within 4 feet of the rim
- Defensively, 1.727 PPP in pick and roll with Stack on the floor

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .player-card title="Trinity Vance" fill="false"}

::: {.player-meta}

**Role:** Spot-up shooter and secondary creator

**Identity:** Movement shooter who can spread the floor and get downhill with ball in her hands

:::

#### Tendencies

- Primary initiator offensively in transition - works to get early paint touch, great at attacking closeouts
- Incredibly quick first step going right especially out of ball screens
- Normally secondary initiator (starts in corner, lifts into ball reversal)

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Guard Her

- Over and trailing everything to force her off the line
- Do not help in gap under the basket and keep track of her on the weakside

:::

#### Numbers

- 1.059 PPP off spot-up play type
- 37% 3-point shooter this season (4/11)
- 0.419 PPP as P&R ball handler on 31 possessions

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .player-card title="Dalanna Carter" fill="false"}

::: {.player-meta}

**Role:** Primary ballhandler and versatile scorer

**Identity:** Downhill attacker who is very patient in the midrange and pushes ball in transition

:::

#### Tendencies

- Can be a corner spacer when off-ball and a great shooter
- Most dynamic and versatile ballhandler, great attacker downhill
- Creative and patient against weakside help

::: {.game-plan}

- Over-drop in ball screens, maintain backside pressure and keep Cat attached to roller
- Pick up full court to stop early paint touches and force offense to slow down

:::

- 5/18 within 4 feet of rim

# Offense

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .concept-card title="High post fills + catches with flow around bigs" fill="false"}

::: {.concept-summary}

**What They Do:** 4-out 1-in spacing with Stack filling at FT line and perimeter action around her

:::

#### How They Do It

- Big exchanges with Carter and Vance initiating paint touches with drive and kick
- Off-ball screens with Stack seals and weakside corner exchanges/lifts

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Defend It

- Maintain high ball pressure and denials against guards to make them work for their downhill attacks
- Stay physical against Stack high post catches and maintain gap principles when they get paint touches

:::

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .concept-card title="Early paint touches + rim runs with bigs" fill="false"}

::: {.concept-summary}

**What They Do:** Work to get Carter and Vance up the floor off makes and misses before defense gets set

:::

#### How They Do It:

- Send Brackens, Stack as trackers to rim run and seal alongside guards
- Try to work early punch action or stampede early in the shot clock to force defense into rotation and gain advantage before halfcourt entry

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Defend It

- Make sure we have at least two back after shot goes up offensively to quarterback the defense getting set
- Deny or front seals in the paint within first 2-3 seconds of possession to force possession to slow down

:::

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .concept-card title="Empty corner ball screens for Vance and Carter" fill="false"}

::: {.concept-summary}

**What They Do:** Use their two best facilitators in tandem to flow into empty corner PnR and find baseline attacks

:::

#### How They Do It:

- Work out of primary halfcourt principles (4-out 1-in, Stack high post) in first half of shot clock to try to work the paint
- Lift weakside corner with secondary ballhandler and flow into empty corner or regular wing PnR later in shot clock

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Defend It

- 1-4 switch to maintain ball pressure on the two ballhandlers and load up the box against baseline attack depending on shooter positions
- Deny catches on everything and try to force secondary ballhandler backdoor to mess up their desired action

:::

# Defense

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .concept-card title="Deep drop coverage with Stack out of ball screens" fill="false"}

::: {.concept-summary}

**What They Do:** Stack stationed as rim protector, basically plays 1v2 out of deep drop coverage

:::

#### How They Do It:

- Maintain ball pressure against screens and force ballhandler into Stack’s length and size
- Have her play 1v2 or peel switch depending on situation but leave midrange mostly open

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Attack It

- Keep defender on hip and take what defense gives (should be plenty of good midrange looks against over-drop)
- Stay wide to open pocket pass for roller and force Stack to move in space

:::

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .concept-card title="1-2-1-1 full court back to 2-3; gap mostly comes from Stack roaming in the paint as rim protector" fill="false"}

::: {.concept-summary}

**What They Do:** Mix in a 1-2-1-1 full court zone press and use Stack to roam off her man instead of playing full team gap help

:::

#### How They Do It:

- Press off dead balls or made free throws unexpectedly to catch opponent off guard; trap first pass and/or first entry into frontcourt
- Give Stack freedom to roam when her man is on perimeter and rotate around her to protect rim effectively

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Attack It

- Stay patient against the press and look to fill middle and get down the floor
- Use Cat in space and as tracker to attack off the catch and force rotation from smaller defenders around Stack

:::

#### Clip Evidence

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .concept-card title="Aggressive weakside collapse on paint touches but solid perimeter denials with disciplined recoveries" fill="false"}

::: {.concept-summary}

**What They Do:** Varying coverages depending matchups but show off-ball pressure with heavy baseline gap presence

:::

#### How They Do It:

- Don’t worry about the weakside and maintain principles of blocking off the paint and forcing kickouts
- Deny the catch above the FT line and force backdoor cuts into stationed big; work to reverse pivot and cut off any potential basket cuts

::: {.game-plan}

#### How I’d Attack It

- Maintain spacing especially out of corners and keep ball popping to force next coverage and rotation

:::

# Final Three Keys

## Row {.flow}

:::: {.card .three-keys title="Final Three Keys" fill="false"}

<div class="keys-grid">

<div class="key-item"><span class="key-number">1</span><strong>Stop early paint touches from Carter and Vance and keep Stack from establishing easy high-post catches.</strong></div>

<div class="key-item"><span class="key-number">2</span><strong>Attack Stack in ball screens, use the space in deep drop, and force her to defend away from the rim.</strong></div>

<div class="key-item"><span class="key-number">3</span><strong>Stay patient against pressure and weakside collapse, maintain spacing, and keep the ball moving to force rotations.</strong></div>

</div>
